tool.name: multiz progressive fold
tool.description: fold per-query pairwise MAFs into one multi-way MAF for a hinge
tool.command:
mkdir -p pairs &&
## The hinge name arrives as the CONTENT of a one-line dataset rather than as a ## text parameter. A workflow that maps this tool over the hinge dimension has ## no way to put a map-over element identifier into a text param -- connecting ## the collection to one yields the repr of a DatasetCollectionElement, which is ## how every fold in the 2026-06-13 runs died on the name validator. HINGE=\$(tr -d '[:space:]' < '$hinge_label') && case "\$HINGE" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) echo "hinge label dataset must hold one strain name (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, dot); got: '\$HINGE'" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac &&
## Stage each pairwise-MAF element under its query strain name ## (element_identifier), prefixing the src names so multiz can tell the two ## species apart -- it splits src on the first '.', so bare contig accessions ## would read as one species per contig. #for $el in $pairwise_mafs python '$__tool_directory__/maf_prefix_srcs.py' --hinge "\$HINGE" --query '${el.element_identifier}' --input '$el' --output 'pairs/${el.element_identifier}.maf' && printf '%s\n' '$el.element_identifier' >> queries.txt && #end for
## Order query strains closest-first by DESCENDING sourmash similarity to the ## hinge (Decision 5: similarity, 1.0 = identical). NOT mash ascending distance. python '$__tool_directory__/multiz_order.py' --compare-csv '$compare_csv' --hinge "\$HINGE" --queries \$(cat queries.txt) > order.txt &&
## Progressive multiz fold: start from the closest query's pairwise MAF, then ## fold each next-closest query's pairwise MAF onto the running MAF ## (multiz prev.maf next.maf 1 > merged), per impl/10_multiz.sh:100-110. PREV='' && while read -r Q; do NEXT="pairs/\${Q}.maf" && if [ -z "\$PREV" ]; then PREV="\$NEXT" ; else NEW=\$(mktemp ./multiz_tmp_XXXXXX.maf) && multiz "\$PREV" "\$NEXT" 1 > "\$NEW" && case "\$PREV" in pairs/*) : ;; *) rm -f "\$PREV" ;; esac && PREV="\$NEW" ; fi ; done < order.txt &&
cp "\$PREV" '$folded_maf'

param.name: pairwise_mafs
param.label: Per-query pairwise MAFs for this hinge
param.help: A 'list' collection of the hinge's pairwise alignments (hinge vs each query). The element identifier MUST be the query strain name and the hinge must be the reference (top) row in every block.

param.label: sourmash compare.csv similarity matrix
param.help: N+1 row sourmash compare.csv (header of strain labels, then one similarity row per strain). Similarity is 1.0 = identical; fold order sorts DESCENDING (closest first).

param.name: hinge_label
param.label: Hinge strain name (one-line dataset)
param.help: A text dataset whose contents are the hinge strain name, e.g. a single line reading PvW1. It must appear as a label in compare.csv. This is a dataset rather than a text box so that a workflow mapping over the hinge dimension can supply one name per job -- Galaxy cannot route a map-over element identifier into a text parameter.

tool.help:
**multiz progressive fold** — build one multi-way MAF for a hinge strain.
[multiz](https://github.com/multiz/multiz) (part of TBA) merges *pairwise* MAF block sets that share a common reference. This tool ports the per-hinge progressive fold from the *Pv4* pangenome pipeline (`impl/10_multiz.sh`): given all of a hinge's pairwise alignments (hinge **H** vs each query **Q**), it grows the multi-way alignment one query at a time, threading every new query through what is already aligned onto **H**'s coordinate scaffold.
-----
**Fold order matters.** multiz threads each new strain transitively through the running alignment, so a distant strain folded early loses blocks that fail to thread. The queries are therefore folded **closest-first**, ordered by **descending** sourmash similarity to the hinge read from `compare.csv` (Decision 5: sourmash reports *similarity*, 1.0 = identical — so the order is DESC, the opposite of the mash *distance* convention).
The fold then runs iteratively:
``` multiz prev.maf next.maf 1 > merged.maf ```
starting from the closest query's pairwise MAF and folding the next-closest each step.
-----
**Inputs**
- *Per-query pairwise MAFs* — a `list` collection of the hinge's pairwise alignments. The **element identifier is the query strain name**, and the hinge must be the reference (top) row of every block. - *compare.csv* — the sourmash N×N similarity matrix used to order the fold. - *Hinge strain name* — a one-line text dataset holding the reference strain name, which must be a label in `compare.csv`. It is a dataset rather than a text box because a workflow maps this tool over the hinge dimension and Galaxy cannot route a map-over element identifier into a text parameter; connecting a collection to one substitutes the repr of the element object.
-----
**src names.** multiz decides which species a row belongs to by reading the text before the first `.` in the MAF `src` field, so every row must arrive as `strain.contig`. `axtToMaf` writes whatever the AXT carried, which for chained alignments is a bare contig accession such as `QMFC01000014.1` — one species per contig as far as multiz is concerned. This tool therefore rewrites the src names as it stages each pairwise MAF, taking the target row's strain from the hinge and the query row's from the element identifier. A src that already carries the right prefix is left alone.
**Output**
- `{hinge}.multiz.maf` — a single multi-way MAF whose blocks carry the hinge plus every query that threaded.
-----
Ported from `Pv4-pangenome/v3/pipeline/impl/10_multiz.sh`. The upstream pairwise AXT→MAF step (`axtToMaf`, IUC `ucsc_axtomaf`) is **not** part of this tool.
